note.label: Ezra 2: The Register of Those Who Returned

precepts.why:
Zerubbabel, who led the first wave up out of the captivity with Jeshua, Nehemiah and the other chief men, had been one of the bodyguards of the Persian Empire. In 1 Esdras he is the wisest of the guards, and the king tells him, “Ask what thou wilt more than is appointed in the writing, and we will give it thee, because thou art found wisest; and thou shalt sit next me, and shalt be called my cousin.”

That is how the children of the province came to go up: the king granted Zerubbabel his request above what he asked, and the men whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away unto Babylon “came again unto Jerusalem and Judah, every one unto his city”, with Zerubbabel at their head.

precepts.text: All Israel was reckoned by genealogies written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
precepts.point: The priests who could not find their register by genealogy were put from the priesthood as polluted, forbidden the most holy things until a priest stood up with Urim and Thummim.

note.label: Ezra 2: The Register of Those Who Returned

precepts.why:
“So all Israel were reckoned by genealogies; and, behold, they were written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, who were carried away to Babylon for their transgression.” Israel kept its register: every man's father's house and seed was written down, and the book went with them into the captivity.

That is why those from Tel-melah, Tel-harsa, Cherub, Addan and Immer, who “could not shew their father’s house, and their seed, whether they were of Israel”, were set aside. And the children of the priests who “sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy” and were not found were “as polluted, put from the priesthood”, forbidden to eat of the most holy things “till there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim.” The genealogy was the proof of who was Israel, and without it a man could not stand in the priesthood.

points: These are the children of the province who came up out of captivity, whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away, returning each man to his own city in Jerusalem and Judah.
